name: How chips get so small

hook_variants.template: Your phone in your pocket? It holds 16 billion tiny switches.
{news_title} Behind it: silicon printed three nanometers wide.
Sixteen billion transistors in one chip. That's modern silicon.

sections.text: Behind every gadget sits a wafer of silicon, carved atom by atom.
A flagship chip packs 16 billion tiny switches.
sections.subtitle: transistors — Apple M1

sections.text: The parts printed on it shrank from 45 nanometers to just 3.
sections.title: Chip feature size (nm)

sections.text: They print it by flashing ultraviolet light through one stencil, then another, hundreds of times.
One of those printing machines costs over a hundred million dollars.
sections.title: EUV lithography

sections.text: Every chip you own went through this. Follow for more tech explainers.
